items.stem: In Dash, what does a callback's Output specify?

options.text: Which component property is updated when the callback runs
options.rationale: Correct: an Output names the component and property the return value updates.

options.text: The initial layout of the application
options.rationale: Layout is defined separately, not by the callback Output.

options.text: The server port the app runs on
options.rationale: That is a run configuration, not a callback Output.

options.text: The CSS theme of the page
options.rationale: Styling is unrelated to the callback Output declaration.

items.explanation: Correct: an Output names the component and property the return value updates.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep a data-heavy Dash app responsive? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Aggregate or sample data server-side before sending it to the browser
options.rationale: Correct: smaller payloads render faster and use less memory.

options.text: Cache the results of expensive, repeated queries
options.rationale: Correct: caching avoids recomputing the same expensive result.

options.text: Send the full raw dataset to every client on load
options.rationale: Large payloads slow the browser and the network.

options.text: Trigger a callback on every keystroke in a text box without debouncing

items.explanation: Correct: smaller payloads render faster and use less memory.

items.stem: When should you reach for Plotly graph objects instead of Plotly Express?

options.text: When you need fine-grained control over individual traces and layout that Express does not expose directly
options.rationale: Correct: graph objects give lower-level control for complex figures.

options.text: Only when the dataset is small
options.rationale: Dataset size is not the deciding factor.

options.text: Never; Express can do everything graph objects can with less effort
options.rationale: Express is convenient but does not expose every low-level option.

options.text: Whenever you want a static image only
options.rationale: Static export works from either interface.

items.explanation: Correct: graph objects give lower-level control for complex figures.
